Recommended Optimizations

Maximize Clicks Delivering — $4,459 Spent, 42,141 Clicks

Both campaigns are spending steadily with stable CPCs. Combined spend is $4,459 (44.6% of $10,000 budget) with 42,141 total clicks at a blended $0.106 CPC.

Invesco: $3,033 / $7,500 (40.4%) · $0.104 CPC Capital One: $1,426 / $2,500 (57.0%) · $0.109 CPC

Capital One is at 57% spent and on pace to fully deliver. Invesco has spent 40.4% with $4,467 remaining.

Invesco: Mid-Majors Article Dominating — Concentration Risk

One article is consuming 41.8% of all clicks and 41.8% of spend:

Mid-Majors Lobby: 6,365 clicks · 7.41% CTR · $685 spend

Two other articles are performing well but at much lower scale:

UNC/Hubert Davis: 2,983 clicks · 10.22% CTR · $300 spend Cinderellas Are Rich: 2,125 clicks · 2.89% CTR · $234 spend

Action: With March Madness ending, add fresh Final Four and post-tournament content to the rotation. The UConn Final Four article (578 clicks, 5.25% CTR) is a strong early signal — feed it more budget. Also note the NCAA/DraftKings article remains disapproved (0 impressions) — remove or replace it.

Capital One: Excellent Distribution Across 17 Articles

No single article exceeds 10.8% of clicks — a major improvement from the original 76% concentration. Top performer is Mets/$370M Payroll at 1,141 clicks, with Augusta/Masters (1,070) and MLB Season (1,026) close behind.

High-CTR performers:

Jack Nicklaus: 9.21% CTR · 109 clicks Tiger Woods DUI: 6.69% CTR · 953 clicks Tiger/TGL (paused): 7.11% CTR · 1,275 clicks

With 57.0% of budget spent, the remaining $1,074 should comfortably deliver through the flight. Keep refreshing articles to maintain CTR as content ages.

Capital One: CPC Stable at $0.110 — Monitor Low-CTR Tail

CPC ticked down from $0.114 to $0.110 — no inflation despite scaling. A few articles are running higher CPCs that could be trimmed if budget needs to stretch:

Hornets/Padel: 1.37% CTR · $0.128 CPC Denver Summit: 1.47% CTR · $0.140 CPC UVA Women's: 2.55% CTR · $0.150 CPC

Fidelity / F1: Pre-Launch Setup (Based on Learnings)

1. Launch with Maximize Clicks from day one — both active campaigns confirmed this works. 2. Seed with 8+ articles minimum — Capital One's healthy 17-article mix is the model to follow. 3. Layer multiple audience segments — Google Signals (crypto/finance interest) + behavioral (sports biz readers) + contextual (F1 content). 4. Cross-functional: Editorial can front-load F1 content in late March. Social can amplify organically. Sales can use the Toyota case study to set delivery expectations.

Note on Toyota Data

The Toyota/Olympics campaign was the first use of this tactic. Back-end ad impression tracking via GA4 was not fully in place during the flight, so the ad impressions figure (57,785) is a retroactive estimate from the GA4 data pulled for March. The front-end Google Ads data (clicks, CTR, CPC, spend) is complete and accurate. Current campaigns now have full end-to-end tracking in place.

How This Works — For Sales / AM Reference

We use a portion of the partner's campaign budget to run Google Demand Gen ads driving traffic to FOS articles contextually relevant to the advertiser's campaign. This traffic generates ad impressions for the partner's ads on that content. The result: accelerated campaign delivery with contextually targeted, high-engagement impressions.

Maximize Clicks Working — Campaign Spending

Spend reached $3,033 (40.4% of budget). CPC settled at $0.104 — higher than the manual $0.05 but delivering 29,064 clicks with a strong 4.93% CTR. The algorithm is optimizing efficiently.

Mid-Majors Article Concentration Risk

The Mid-Majors Lobby article is consuming 41.8% of all clicks and spend ($685). While it has a strong 7.41% CTR, this is a single-article dependency. With March Madness ending, this article's performance will decline.

Action: Add fresh Final Four and post-tournament content immediately. The UConn Final Four article (578 clicks, 5.25% CTR) is a strong signal — scale it. Also remove the NCAA/DraftKings article — it's been disapproved by Google and has 0 impressions.

Budget Pacing: $4,467 Remaining

At 40.4% spent with the March Madness flight ending, there's significant budget left. The next content refresh is critical — without new articles, daily spend will decline as existing March Madness content ages out of relevance.

On Pace to Fully Deliver — $1,426 of $2,500 Spent (57.0%)

CPC improved to $0.109. With 13,077 clicks across 17 articles, this campaign has the healthiest article distribution of any Demand Gen flight. The algorithm is spending efficiently.

Tiger Woods DUI Scaling as New Top Performer

The Tiger Woods DUI article has scaled from 492 to 953 clicks at 6.69% CTR — becoming a top-3 performer. Augusta/Masters (1,070 clicks) and Mets (1,141 clicks) are also delivering strong volume. Evergreen sports-business content is performing well for the SMB audience.

Remaining $1,074 — Trim or Maintain?

With 43% of the budget remaining, the current article mix should comfortably deliver. Two options:

Maintain: Keep the current 17-article mix running. The algorithm will naturally weight toward top performers.

Trim for efficiency: Pause the lowest-CTR tail to concentrate budget on higher performers: Hornets/Padel: 1.37% CTR Denver Summit: 1.47% CTR Pittsburgh/Draft: 1.54% CTR (already paused)

Pre-Launch Recommendations

Launch Checklist (Based on Toyota, Invesco & Capital One Learnings)

1. Use Maximize Clicks from day one — set daily budget cap aligned to total budget ÷ flight days. Do not use manual CPC bidding.

2. Seed with 6+ articles minimum — Capital One showed the risk of over-indexing on one article (76% concentration). Build a diverse F1 content pool before launch.

3. Layer multiple audience segments — Google Signals (crypto/finance interest) + behavioral (sports biz readers) + contextual (F1 content). Let the algo optimize across them.

4. Cross-functional leverage: Editorial can front-load F1 content production in late March. Social can amplify organically to compound paid traffic. Sales can use the Toyota case study to set expectations with Fidelity on delivery timeline.

This campaign ended on February 23, 2026. Data is preserved for benchmarking and reporting.

Toyota / Olympics — Final Summary

Top performer: "Figure Skating Music Copyright" — 53.9K clicks at 5.99% CTR.

Efficiency: $0.059 blended CPC delivered 118.6K clicks on a $7K budget. Campaign traffic accounted for 34.5% of total article pageviews, directly fueling Toyota ad delivery on Olympics content.

This campaign is the benchmark for pacing, CPC, and delivery expectations across all future Demand Gen campaigns.
